title: #23. The Battle Of Badr Part 3
arabic:
السلام عليكم ورحمة اللهِ و بركاته اَعُوْذُ بِاللهِ مِنَّ الشِّيْطَانِ الرَّجِيْمِ ۝ بِسْمِ اللهِ الرَّحْمَانِ الرَّحِيْمَ ۝

اَلْحَمْدُ لله ، وَالصَّلَاةُ وَالسَّلَامُ عَلى سَيِّدِنَا محمد وَعَلَى اَلِهِ وَصَحْبِهِ وَسَلِّمْ تَسْلِيْمًا كَثِيْراَ هَذَالَّذِيْ فَعَلَ بنا الْأفَاعيْلْ

اَسَدْ الله ورسوله لَوْ كَانَ المُطْعَمْ بِنْ عُدَيْ حَيًّا ثُمَّ كَلَّمَنِيَّ فِيْ هَؤُلَآءِ النَّتَنْى لَتَرَكْتُهُمْ لًهْ لِعَدَوَتِكَ لِلهِ وَرَسُوْلِه

فَمَنْ لِّسِّبِيَّهْ قَدِّمْه’ يَا عَاصِمْ اَضْرِبْ عُنُقَهْ اِسْتَوْصُوْا اَسَرَى خَيْرًا كُنْتُ فِيْ الْأَسَارَى يَوْمَ بَدْرٍ، فَقَالَ رَسُول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم اِسْتَوْصُوْ بِلْاَسَرَى خَيْرًا

وَكُنْتُ فِيْ نَفَرٍ مِنَّ الْأَنْصَارِ فَكَانُوْا إِذَا قَدّمُوْا عَشَاءَهُمْ اَوْغَدَاءَهُمْ أَكَّلُوْا التَّمْرَ وَاَطْعَمُوْنِيْ الْبُرَّة (خَصّونِي بالخبز) ؛ لِوَصِيَّةِ رَسول الله

كُنْتُ فِيْ رَاهط مِّنَّ الْاَنْصَارِ جَزَآءَهُمُ اللهُ خَيْرًا كُنَّا اِذَ تَعَشَّيْنَا اَوْ تَغَدَّيْنَا آثرُوْنِيْ بِالخُبْزْ وَكَانُوْ يَحْمِلُوْنَنَا وَيَمْشُوْنْ

Rasool Ullah صلوات الله وسلام عليه said; اَمَّا ظَاهِرُكَ فَكَانَ عَلَيْنَا لا اله الا الله يَا أَيُّهَا النَّبِيُّ قُلْ لِمَنْ فِي أَيْدِيكُمْ مِنَ الْأَسْرَىٰ

إِنْ يَعْلَمِ اللَّهُ فِي قُلُوبِكُمْ خَيْرًا يُؤْتِكُمْ خَيْرًا مِمَّا أُخِذَ مِنْكُمْ وَيَغْفِرْ لَكُمْ ۗ وَاللَّهُ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ ّ۝

وَإِنْ يُرِيدُوا خِيَانَتَكَ فَقَدْ خَانُوا اللَّهَ مِنْ قَبْلُ فَأَمْكَنَ مِنْهُمْ ۗ وَاللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ حَكِيمٌ۝

يَا مَعْشَرَقُرَيْشْ لَا تَكُوْنُوْا آخِرَ النَّاسِ اِسْلَامًا وَاَوَّلَّهُمْ رِدَّةْ مَنْ رَابَنَا ضَرَبْنَا عُنُقَا اِقْرَأْ بِاسْمِ رَبِّكَ الَّذِي خَلَقَ

فِيْهِ اَلْهُدَى مَا تَعُدُّوْنَ اَهْلَ بَدْرٍ فِيْكُمْ وَإِذَا لَقُوا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا قَالُوا آمَنَّا وَإِذَا خَلَوْا إِلَىٰ شَيَاطِينِهِمْ قَالُوا إِنَّا مَعَكُمْ إِنَّمَا نَحْنُ مُسْتَهْزِئُونَ۝

عمت صباحا اَلسلام عليكم ورحمة الله تَبَّتْ الَّهَا مِنْ سُيُوْفُهَا الْاَغْنَتْ عَنَّا شَيْاً اَشْهَدُ اَنَّكَ رَسُوْلُ الله Allahعَزّوجَلّ says;

وَمَا جَعَلَهُ اللَّهُ إِلَّا بُشْرَىٰ لَكُمْ وَلِتَطْمَئِنَّ قُلُوبُكُمْ بِهِ ۗ وَمَا النَّصْرُ إِلَّا مِنْ عِنْدِ اللَّهِ الْعَزِيزِ الْحَكِيمِ۝

فَلَمْ تَقْتُلُوهُمْ وَلَٰكِنَّ اللَّهَ قَتَلَهُمْ ۚ وَمَا رَمَيْتَ إِذْ رَمَيْتَ وَلَٰكِنَّ اللَّهَ رَمَىٰ ۚ إن لَقينا إلا عجائزَ صُلعًا إِنَّمَا أُوتِيتُهُ عَلَىٰ عِلْمٍ عِنْدِي ۚ

وَاذْكُرُوا إِذْ أَنْتُمْ قَلِيلٌ مُسْتَضْعَفُونَ فِي الْأَرْضِ تَخَافُونَ أَنْ يَتَخَطَّفَكُمُ النَّاسُ فَآوَاكُمْ وَأَيَّدَكُمْ بِنَصْرِهِ وَرَزَقَكُمْ مِنَ الطَّيِّبَاتِ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَشْكُرُونَ۝

إِنَّ الَّذِينَ تَوَفَّاهُمُ الْمَلَائِكَةُ ظَالِمِي أَنْفُسِهِمْ قَالُوا فِيمَ كُنْتُمْ ۖ قَالُوا كُنَّا مُسْتَضْعَفِينَ فِي الْأَرْضِ ۚ قَالُوا أَلَمْ تَكُنْ أَرْضُ اللَّهِ وَاسِعَةً فَتُهَاجِرُوا فِيهَا ۚ

فَأُولَٰئِكَ مَأْوَاهُمْ جَهَنَّمُ ۖ وَسَاءَتْ مَصِيرًا۝

Allahعَزّوجَلّ said; يَا يَحْيَىٰ خُذِ الْكِتَابَ بِقُوَّةٍ ۖ خُذُوا مَا آتَيْنَاكُم بِقُوَّةٍ يَاْتِي السَّهَمْ يَرْمِيْ بِهِ فَيُصِيْب اَحَدُهُمْ فَيَقْتُلُ اَوْ يَضْرِبْ عُنُقُهُ فَيُقْتَلْ

صَلَّى الله عَلى سَيَّدِنَا محمد وَعَلى اَلِهِ وَ صَحْبِهِ وَسَلمْ وَالسلام عليكم ورحمة الله وبركاته
english:
The Life of Muhammadﷺ, The Madinan Period, Volume 1 By Imam Anwar Al_Awlaki, One thing that I forgot to mention when I was talking about the story of the capture of Ummayyah Bin Khalaf(اُمَيَّة بن خَلَف)

by Abdur Rahman Ibn Auf(عبدالرحمن إبن عوف), When he was held captive by Abdur Rahman Ibn Auf(عبدالرحمن إبن عوف) and they were walking through the site of the Battle of Badr(بدر).

Ummayyah(أمَيَّة) asked Abdur Rahman(عبدالرحمن), he said; who was that man, who had an ostrich feather across his chest?

So, Abdur Rahman Ibn Auf(عبدالرحمن إبن عوف) said, that is Hamza Bin Abdul Muttalib رضي الله عنه, Ummayyah Bin Khalaf(اُمَيَّة بن خَلَف) said;

This is the man who ruined us.

So, Hamza Bin Abdul Muttalib(حمزه بن عبدالمطلب) was truly the lion of Allah, The lion of Allah and His messenger, that's something that I just forgot to mention, when I was talking about Ummayyah(أمَيَّه).

We're gonna carry on, with the prisoners of war, we're still talking about that.

Rasool Allah ﷺ says in a Hadith(حديث) narrated by Abu Dawood(ابوداؤد), Rasool Allah ﷺ says if Mut'am Ibn Udaye(مطعم إبن عدي) was still alive,

and he talked to me about these prisoners of war, actually Rasool Allah ﷺ used the word Natan(نتن).

Natan(نتن) means something that has a foul smell.

That is the name that he used to refer to these prisoners of war.

Now probably doesn't literally mean that they were foul smelling, but what is meant by it is that disbelief is foul smelling, figuratively speaking,

because Allah has called it Rijs(رجس), impurity so disbelief is an impure thing.

Anyway, Rasool Allah ﷺ is saying the meaning of the Hadith(حديث).

If Mut'am Ibn Udaye(مطعم إبن عدي), If he was alive, and he interceded for these prisoners of war, I would have released them, for him.

Rasool Allah ﷺ is telling us that he was grateful to Al-Mut'am Ibn Udaye(المطعم إبن عدي).

Who was a disbeliever because of his honesty and his good stand towards the Muslims, even though he was a Mushrik(مشرك) a disbelievers.

And this shows that Rasool Allah ﷺ would act appropriately, according to the deeds of a person.

So, he would deal with good people Kindly and he would deal with evil people accordingly.

Now, we don't want to go into either extreme of being incapable of showing nothing but brutality towards the Kuffar(كفار) or on the other hand to act in a way that only shows that we are interested in appeasing the Kuffar(كفار).

A Muslim should act in each situation and make a judgment in that situation according to what is the most wise method of action.

And one should overcome emotions and one should overcome doing something because of, I'm worried what other people will say, I'm worried, how our perception will be seen.

I'm worried that I will be giving Islam, a bad picture, I'm worried about this, I'm worried about that.

We should forget about all of these considerations and do what is right So, Rasool Allah ﷺ is saying here if this man was alive, I would have released these prisoners of war for him.

On the other hand, Rasool Allah ﷺ, specifically chose Uqba Bin Abi Moait(عقبة بن أبي معيط) and An-Nadhar Bin Haris(نضر بن حارث) to be executed

from among all of the other prisoners of war, which totaled 70.

The number of prisoners of war was 70.

Rasool Allah ﷺ calls Uqba Bin Abi Moait(عقبة بن أبي معيط), and Uqba Bin Abi Moait(عقبة بن أبي معيط) said; How come, O Messenger of Allah you are choosing me out of everyone else to be killed.

O messenger of Allah, if you're gonna kill the rest of the prisoners of war then kill me with them, if you're gonna ransom them, than ransom me with them.

How come you are picking me out of everyone else to be executed?

Rasool Allah ﷺ said; Because of your animosity towards Allah and His messenger.

So, Uqba(عُقْبَة) said; Who will take care of my children.?

Rasool Allah ﷺ told him, the fire.

O Asim(عاصم) Pull him forward and behead him.

And he was promptly beheaded by Asim Bin Thabit رضي الله عنه.

While An-Nadhar Bin Haris(النضر بن حارث) also, Rasool Allah ﷺ, told Ali Ibn Abi Talib(علي ابن ابي طالب) to execute him.

These two men were specifically handpicked, out of everyone else because of their evil and Ibn Kathir رضي الله عنه said; I would comment that these two men were among the most evil of Allah's servants,

the most stubborn, wicked, envious and disbelieving of men and they had been very active in satirizing Islam and its supporters, Allah damn them, and he did, indeed.

Uqba Bin Abi Moait(عقبة بن أبي معيط) was the one who saw Rasool Allah ﷺ in Sujood(سجود) next to Al-Ka'aba(اَلْكَعْبَه), when Rasool Allah ﷺ was still in Makkah

and he stepped over his neck with his foot.

Rasool Allah ﷺ said, I felt that my eyes were going to pop out I was gonna die.

And this is also the man who saw me in Rukkoo(ركوع) and came in threw the intestines of a camel, he threw them over my back and then Fatimah رضي الله عنها came and remove them.

So, Uqba Bin Abi Moait(عقبة بن أبي معيط) was one of the worst devils of Quraish(قُرَيْشْ).

And that is why he deserved this severe punishment.

While An-Nadhar Bin Haris(النضر بن حارث) was the one who went to Persia, to learn the stories of Asfandyaar(أسفند يار) and Rustum(رستم), and he would come back to Makkah, and tell the people to gather around him and he would say,

come and listen to my stories, they're better than Muhammad(محمد)'s stories.

what makes him more befitting to being a prophet compared to me?

He said, I can tell stories just like he could.

So, what makes him entitled to becoming a prophet, and doesn't give me that right.?

So, he used to sway the people away from the Majlis(مجلس) circle of Rasool Allah ﷺ.

So, these two men were executed.

So you can contrast this to what Rasool Allah ﷺ said about Al-Mutam Ibn Udae(ألمطعم إبن عدي) and see how Rasool Allah ﷺ would deal differently with different people.

Now, with these two men, they were executed.

However, with the rest, Rasool Allah ﷺ specifically gave the instructions to the Sahabah رضي الله عنهم and said; Treat the prisoners of war kindly,

treat them kindly.

So, Abu Aziz(ابو عزيز), the brother of Mus'ab Bin Umair(مصعب إبن عمير) he said; He said, I was with a group of Ansaar(اَنْصَار), bringing me from Badr(بدر),

when they had their lunch and dinner, they would give me the bread and ate the dates themselves, in accordance with instruction given them by Rasool Allah ﷺ regarding us,

every piece of bread that came into their hands, they passed on to me, I was embarrassed and would return the bread, but they would pass it back untouched.

Bread was the better food compared to dates, so they would eat the dates and they would give him the bread.

And they would just survive on eating dates.

So, they would give him actually they would give him a better treatment, than they would give themselves.

Ibn Hishaam(إبن هشام), he comments on this. He said; This Abu Aziz(ابوعزيز) was the standard bearer of the Mushrikeen(مشركين) at Badr(بدر), following An-Nadhar Bin Haris(النضر بن حارث).

So, Abu Aziz(ابوعزيز) wasn't just a foot soldier Abu Aziz(ابو عزيز) was the standard bearer on the Battle of Badr(بدر) and still Rasool Allah ﷺ has told to treat such men, well.

Abul Aas Bin Ar-Rabiy(ابوالعاص بن الربيع), he said; Pretty much the same thing.

Al-Waleed Bin Waleed Bin Mugheera(ألوليد بن وليد بن مغيرة), he would say; They would walk while we would ride.

So, the prisoners of war are riding, while the Sahabah رضي الله عنهم are walking.

And Subhaan Allah(سُبْحَان الله), see this good treatment is what caused many of these prisoners of war to become Muslim.

Throughout the battles of Rasool Allah ﷺ, we would hear about people who were arrested or captured and then they would become Muslim and stayed behind.

And some of them to show and prove that they're not becoming Muslim for fear of the sword.

After they are released, they would go back to their people and then they would come back to Rasool Allah ﷺ and become Muslim.

To prove that we have became Muslim of our own initiative, not because any pressure, we weren't pressured into it.

For example, Abu Aziz(ابو عزيز), he ended up becoming Muslim.

The brother of Mus'ab Ibn Umair(مصعب ابن عمير), when he saw, how the Muslims were treating him.

They would treat him better than their own selves So, Akhlaaq(أخلاق) are important even with your enemy, even with the enemy, the Muslim should deal with him, in a good way with dignity.

I mean, a Muslim is not cruel, a Muslim is not wicked, a Muslim is not deceptive, a Muslim is not a liar, a Muslim deals with everyone with honesty, dignity, straightforwardness

and kindness towards all of the creation of Allahعَزّوجَلّ, except those who deserve to be dealt cruelly like Uqba Bin Abi Moait(عقبة بن أبي معيط), and An-Nadhar Bin Haris(النضر بن حارث)

because these are people who are so evil you can't afford, treating them kindly, treating them kindly is actually being fooled by them, because these are people who are going to turn around and harm the Muslims.

Al-Abbas Ibn Abdul Muttalib(العباس بن عبدالمطلب), the uncle of Rasool Allah ﷺ, Ransom yourself, pay your ransom.

Al-Abbas(العباس) said, O Messenger of Allah, I'm a Muslim.

Rasool Allah ﷺ told him; What was evident was that you were against us.

Allah knows best about your accepting Islam.

Rasool Allah ﷺ is here setting for us, a rule, We go by what we see.

We do not and cannot know what is in the hearts.

Only Allahعَزّوجَلّ is, the One, Who can see the hearts, we go by what we see. R asool Allah ﷺ is telling Al-Abbas(العباس), Allah is the one who knows whether you're Muslim or not,

what we can see is that you were against us, you were fighting us, you were in the army of the enemy.

So, we're going to go by that and Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمرابن الخطاب), he said, when he was Khalifah(خليفه), In the time of Rasool Allah ﷺ, Revelation would come down and tell us, what is in the hearts of men.

But now we're going to go by what we see.

We're going to make our judgments based on what appears from you.

If what appears from you is Islam, we will accept that, and if what appears from you is disbelief, we will assume that you are disbeliever, even if you claim that you are otherwise.

If your actions are those of a disbeliever it doesn't benefit you to say that you are a Muslim, We will go by your actions.

So, the action of Al-Abbas(العباس) here was, that he was with the enemy You can claim that you are a Muslim, you can state; But why were you on the enemies side.?

And this is a very important rule, we should not judge people, according to what is in their hearts, we judge them by their action.

In the same time, we don't allow people to fool us by stating, that they are this and that when their actions prove otherwise.

we go by the actions of people that is how we judge people.

So, somebody who's acting as a disbeliever in and out, cannot come on fool us and trick us and say; I'm a Muslim Al-Abbas(العباس) said; I don't have any money.

Rasool Allahﷺ told him; What about the money that you buried in the ground, and you told your wife, Ummal-Fadhal(أم الفضل), if I am killed, then make use of this money.

Al-Abbas(العباس) said: I testify and bear witness that you are a messenger of Allah, no one knew of that treasure of mine, except me and my wife.

So, he did pay for his ransom.

And Allahعَزّوجَلّ revealed the Ayah(آية); O Prophet, say to whoever is in your hands of the captives.

If Allah knows any good in your hearts, He will give you better than what was taken from you, and He will forgive you and Allah's Forgiving and Merciful.

But if they intend to betray you, Then they have already betrayed Allah before and he empowered you over them and Allah is Knowing and Wise.

So, Allahعَزّوجَلّ is telling these, men who claim that they were Muslim and they had to pay for the ransom.

If you are Muslim, Allahعَزّوجَلّ will replace that money that was taken from you, Don't worry.!

Al-Abbas(العباس) said that I paid 20 Uoqia(أوقيه) of gold.

This is a certain weight of gold, I paid that for my ransom.

And then Allahعَزّوجَلّ has given me much more than that.

Meaning Allahعَزّوجَلّ has replaced that money that he paid for ransom and Allahعَزّوجَلّ has multiplied it for Al-Abbas Bin Abdul Muttalib رضي الله عنه.

Abul Aas(ابو العاص) was the husband of Zainab(زينب) Bint(بنت) Rasool Allah ﷺ.

He was a Mushrik(مشرك), so the daughter of Rasool Allah ﷺ up until that point was married to a disbelievers.

This was before the ruling came down preventing Muslim women from remaining with their disbelieving husbands, this was before that ruling.

And she was in Makkah, so she wants to free her husband, Zainab(زينب) Bint Rasool Allah ﷺ, she wants to free her husband Al-Aas(ألعاص).

So, let me read to you what Ibn Is'haaq(ابن اسحاق) said about this situation.

Actually, I will read you the story of her coming back.

But before that let's just talk about the ransoming.

So, Zainabرضي الله عنها , she sends an amount of money sufficient to release her husband from captivity.

She also sends along with that money a necklace.

This necklace was given to her as a gift by her mother Khadijah(خديجه), when she got married.

This was her wedding gift, from her mother.

So, the necklace belonged to Khadijah(خديجه) and then Khadijah(خديجه) gave it as a gift to her daughter when she got married.

So, Zainab(زينب) sends this necklace.

When the necklace falls in the hands of Rasool Allah ﷺ, it brought back memories of his wife Khadijah رحمة الله عليها, and we know that Rasool Allah ﷺ was very soft hearted, kind, compassionate and this touched him.

So, Rasool Allah ﷺ told the Ansaar(أنصار) who were holding her husband.

He said: If you should think fit to deliver her prisoner to her, and to return to her, what is hers then do so.

And they immediately released him and they released them without ransom.

And they sent back also the necklace.

Now Rasool Allah ﷺ, placed a condition on the release of Abul Aas(ابوالعاص).

And that condition was you never assist an enemy against us, and you send to me, Zainab(زينب).

So, Abul Aas(ابوالعاص) was a man of his word.

When he went back to Makkah He allowed Zainab(زينب) to leave Makkah and go to her father.

Ibn Is'haaq says; so she continued making plans.

When she was ready, her husband's brother, Kinanah Ibn Rabiyah(كنانة إبن ربيعه) brought a camel which she mounted.

And he taking his bow and quiver, led her away.

She riding in a Haudaj(هودج), and it being daytime.

Some of the Quraish(قُرَيْشْ) men discussed this and followed after her catching up with her Dhu Tuwaa(ذو طوى), the first to reach her was Habbar Ibn Aswad Ibn Al-Muttalib(هبار إبن أسود إبن المطلب).

He scared her with his spear as she was there in the Haudaj(هودج).

And because as they claimed, she was pregnant at the time, she suffered a miscarriage.

Her brother in law then knelt down and took the arrows from his quiver, saying, By Allah, if any man comes near me, I'll put an arrow into him,

the man drew away from him.

Then Abu Sufiyan(ابوسفيان) arrived with some other Quraish(قُرَيْشْ) leaders and said, Put down your arrows, so we can talk with you.

He did so and Abu Sufiyan(ابوسفيان) drew near him and said; You have not done well.

You came forth with a woman openly going over people's heads, even though you're aware of the injury and damage done us by Muhammad(محمد).

We ask Allahعَزّوجَلّ to forgive us all, to grant us Jannah(جنة).

And we ask Him to spare us, from the punishment of hellfire.

Another lesson; Istighasah(إستغاثه) seeking assistance from Allah.

Rasool Allah ﷺ, after he prepared the army, and train them and lined them up and gave them his instructions and chose the best location.

After all of that, he went aside and he started making Dua(دعا).

And that is the meaning of Tawakkul(توكل).

Tawakkul(توكل) means that you do your best.

You exhaust the worldly means, and then you depend on Allahعَزّوجَلّ.

So, Rasool Allah ﷺ, he did his best, in terms of everything that he was capable of doing, in this world in terms of preparing for this battle.

And after that, he started making Dua(دُعَا) to Allahعَزّوجَلّ.

So, don't think that Allah will give you victory.

If you sit at home comfortable on your couch and just raise your hands and say O Allah, give me victory, O Allah give them victory, O Allah give the Muslim Ummah(امة) victory.

You have to stand up and do something, you have to do your best and then you ask Allahعَزّوجَلّ to give you, and this applies to everything,

This is the issue of Tawakkul(توكل).

You know, some people have an understanding of Tawakkul(توكل) that is not really Tawakkul(توكل), this is what is called Tawaakul(تواكل), like those whom were walking lazily, you know, pretending as if they are Zuhaad(زهاد).

And Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمر ابن الخطاب) saw them, he said: Who are these?

They said these are Al-Muttawakkiloon(ألمتوكلون).

These are the ones, who have Tawakkal(توكل) in Allah.

So, he went and beat them with his stick and said; you know that the sky doesn't rain, gold and silver, you have to go out and work.

So the meaning of Tawakkul(توكل) is what Rasool Allah ﷺ mentioned in the Hadith(حديث), he said if you have the right Tawakkul(توكل) on Allah,

Allah will give you, provide for you, like he provides for the birds, they leave in the morning hungry and they come back at evening full.

So, here the birds didn't stay at home, they went out, worked for the entire day.

And that is the meaning of Tawakkul(توكل).

So, Tawakkul(توكل) is, you do your best but you do not depend on your effort, you do not depend on your intelligence, you do not dependent on anything in this world.

But you depend on Allah.

So Yes, Rasool Allah ﷺ prepared the army, Yes, he lined them up, Yes, he gave them instructions but he didn't depend on that.

He went aside And he started making Dua(دُعَا) and he was so involved in the Dua(دُعَا) and the Dua(دُعَا) was so long, Abu Bakr As-Siddique رضي الله عنه felt sorry for him,

and said: O Rasool Allah, that's enough.

Allah will give you, what He promised to you, Allah already promised you.

So, we have to have Istighasah(إستغاثه) on Allahعَزّوجَلّ, depend on Allahعَزّوجَلّ but you also have to do your best.

So, we don't just do our best and then forget about the Dua(دُعَا).

And we don't just do the Dua(دُعَا) and forget about doing our best, they both go hand in hand.

This is the end of our commentary on the Battle of Badr(بدر).
